1|# Handoff 01 - Claude: core contracts of C3 (ledger, findings, handoff, store, engine)
2|
3|Date: 2026-09-26. Base commit: `e1acae1` (clean tree except this `.collab/c3-core-contract/` directory).
4|
5|## Question
6|
7|Are the core contracts in `crates/c3-core` safe to build the engines (M2c), the ledger runtime (M3) and the `http`
8|path (M7) on? Every dependent milestone hangs on these types and traits; changing them later means rewriting the
9|engine adapters and the store. Review the shapes and invariants, not the prose.
10|
11|## Delta since the last review
12|
13|Follows: the framing panel of task `c3-design` (`.collab/c3-design/handoffs/01..15`, decisions in
14|`.collab/c3-design/state.md`, design of record `docs/DESIGN.md`). This is the first review of the code.

17|- Milestone 2a landed (`e1acae1`): the contracts below, with byte-identical round-trips of the real stores.
18|- The plugin session (working in `../claude-codex-consult`, now at 9d79206) confirmed: the ledger field order comes
19|  from the `$entry` literal and the harness `$order` string; roster gets an `ext` object for C3 data (wave 26);
20|  R12 status-file shape is decided, not frozen.
21|
22|## CURRENT invariants claimed
23|
24|- Files are the record; `.collab/<task>/{sessions.json, findings.json, handoffs/}` are byte-compatible with the
25|  plugin (`ps_json.rs` reproduces Windows PowerShell 5.1 `ConvertTo-Json`; the real c3-design stores, 194 KB and
26|  184 KB, round-trip byte-identically through the typed `SessionsFile` / `FindingsFile`).
27|- `LedgerEntry` carries every field of the wave-24 order string, in that order; `SessionsFile::add_entry` keeps
28|  `consults` sorted by `n`.
29|- Write order is `COMMIT_WRITE_ORDER`: `.reply.json` before the lock; under `.consult.write.lock`: re-read both
30|  stores, apply the delta, write the handoff `.md`, then `findings.json`, then `sessions.json` (commit point),
31|  then remove the pending record, then release. Atomic replace = temp + flush + rename.
32|- A lock is a permanent file owned by holding it open; the record inside is informational; releasing = dropping
33|  the handle. Lock share-mode fidelity and write-lock backoff are NOT in `c3-core` (see Q7).
34|- Finding transitions: any status may follow any other; `verified` needs evidence, `rejected` and a reopen need a
35|  note, `superseded` neither; `history[]` append-only.
36|- Lineage = `provider :: model [engine]` on an endpoint fingerprint; never fork or resume across lineages.
37|- `Engine` for `http`: no tools, no sandbox, no threads (`capabilities(Http)`), `plan()` returns `NoArgv`.
38|- `verdict` (reviewer) and `bridge_outcome` (bridge) are distinct fields; usable outcomes are exactly two strings.
39|- C3 never commits to git. Reviewers are read-only.
40|

42|
43|Base commit `e1acae1`, fingerprint not computed.
44|
45|| File | Change |
46||---|---|
47|| `crates/c3-core/src/ledger.rs` | `SessionsFile`, `LedgerEntry` (asserted order), nested records, `read`/`to_bytes`/`add_entry` |
48|| `crates/c3-core/src/findings.rs` | `FindingsFile`, `Finding`, statuses, `HistoryEvent`, `Rating`, `finding_id`, pure `transition` |

50|| `crates/c3-core/src/store.rs` | `EvidenceStore` trait, `FilesStore`, `LockRecord`, `PendingRecord`, `TaskLock`, `COMMIT_WRITE_ORDER` |
51|| `crates/c3-core/src/engine.rs` | `Engine` trait, `EngineKind`, `Capabilities`, `Request`, `Argv`, `Reply`, `StructuredReply` (deny_unknown_fields), ids, `SubprocessEngine::plan` (exact codex/agy/muse argv) |
52|| `crates/c3-core/src/ps_json.rs` | the PS 5.1 formatter and its rules |
53|| `crates/c3-core/tests/contracts.rs` | byte-identity and header-render acceptance tests |
54|| `docs/port/contracts.md` | contract map, sources, invariants, the 8 questions below in full |
55|| `docs/port/cli-surface.md`, `m2-acceptance.md`, `m3-acceptance.md`, `fake-clis.md` | the port surface the engines will be measured against |
56|
57|## Open findings
58|
59|_(none open in this task; the c3-design findings are design-level and closed by DESIGN.md)_
60|
61|## Requested checks run
62|
63|_(first review of this task)_
64|
65|## Evidence
66|
67|- `crates/c3-core/tests/contracts.rs` - `cargo test`: 42 pass; the two stores re-serialise byte-identically.
68|- `docs/port/contracts.md` - the contract map with plugin line references and the invariants above.
69|- `docs/port/cli-surface.md` "Open questions" - prompt delivery differs per engine (codex/agy on stdin, agy as one
70|  NDJSON line; muse via `--prompt-file` with empty stdin); the muse oauth/billing guard is re-checked before every
71|  secondary turn; timeout continuation, denial retry and format repair are three mechanisms with distinct gating.
72|- `crates/c3-core/src/engine.rs:286-310` - the `Engine` trait: `capabilities()`, `plan(&Request) -> Argv`,
73|  `run(&Request) -> Reply`, `continue_turn(...)`.
74|- `crates/c3-core/src/store.rs:158-190` - the `EvidenceStore` trait: `task_dir`, `read_sessions`, `read_findings`,
75|  `recover_pending`, `next_handoff_number`, `take_task_lock`, `write_pending`, `commit`.
76|
77|## Questions
78|
79|- **Q1.** On-disk JSON is host-dependent in the plugin (PS 5.1 vs PS 7 bytes differ). C3 canonicalises to the 5.1
80|  shape on write and reads any. Is that the right contract for a repository where the plugin (on any host) and C3
81|  both append to one task, or should C3 match the shape of the file it re-reads, or write a clean format and accept
82|  one-time churn?
83|- **Q2.** `Engine` trait shape: is `plan -> Argv` plus `run` / `continue_turn` the right seam when (a) prompt
84|  delivery differs per engine (stdin vs NDJSON line vs `--prompt-file`), (b) `http` has no argv, (c) muse re-checks
85|  its guard before every turn, (d) continuation, denial retry and format repair are three distinct secondary-turn
86|  mechanisms? Propose the minimal change (e.g. a `PromptDelivery` in `Capabilities`, a `Turn` enum, a per-turn
87|  `precheck` hook) rather than a redesign.
88|- **Q3.** Identity: `ConsultationId`, `AttemptId`, `ConversationId` are newtypes over strings. Are the rules
89|  (a retry is a new attempt with the same inputs and no redraw; `http` continuation is replay of pack + prior
90|  reply; lineage never crosses) expressible and enforceable at this layer, or do they belong to the runtime?
91|- **Q4.** The handoff header needs inputs the ledger lacks (provenance phrases, short SHAs, other-lineages list,
92|  roster path and counts, effort basis, severity counts). Should the ledger entry gain fields so a handoff is
93|  regenerable from `sessions.json` alone (breaking the asserted order string), or is a header derived once at write
94|  time and never regenerated the contract?
95|- **Q5.** `usage` is engine-conditional (`total_tokens` only for agy) and `denial_retry`, `timeout_continue`,
96|  `range`, `peak`, `effort_confirmed` are only `null` in the evidence, kept as raw JSON. Accept raw pass-through for
97|  unexercised shapes as the contract until a fixture pins them, or pin them now from the plugin literals?
98|- **Q6.** `http` pack provenance: DESIGN says the pack path and hash ride in `reviewer.provider_config` and a
99|  `.pack.json` sidecar, not a new ledger column (the asserted order string would break). Confirm or contradict.
100|- **Q7.** `EvidenceStore`: lock share-mode fidelity (FileShare.Read on Windows, None on Unix, fail-fast) and the
101|  write-lock backoff with `commit_wait_ms` are deferred to the runtime crate; `c3-core` encodes only the write
102|  order. Right split, or must the trait expose the lock acquisition so the order cannot be bypassed?
103|- **Q8.** What in these contracts will be expensive to change after M2c/M3 build on them and is not covered above
104|  (schema-extension compatibility, worktree identity, cancellation ownership, Windows paths, the R12 status file)?
105|
106|Answer by number. Keep it under 900 words. Cite files by path and line; mark "assumed" where you did not read.

## Q1 — PS 5.1 vs PS 7 bytes
Canonicalise to 5.1 on write, read any. Endorsed: `ps_json.rs:1-30`, byte-identity tests `tests/contracts.rs:45-78`. Churn-free coexistence needs one fixed writer; 5.1 is the only evidence-backed choice. Document it as the wire contract and keep the reader permissive (serde parse + PS formatter only on write). What evidence does not show: a PS 7–written file round-trip; assumed reader accepts it (serde does) but no fixture proves it.

## Q2 — Engine trait seam
`plan -> Argv` + `run` + `continue_turn` is almost right but under-specified. Missing: (a) prompt delivery differs per engine (stdin vs NDJSON line vs `--prompt-file` — see `cli-surface.md` Open questions); `Request.prompt` + `prompt_file: Option` does not say who writes the file or the NDJSON framing. (b) muse per-turn guard re-check has no hook. (c) continuation vs denial-retry vs format-repair are distinct but `continue_turn(conversation, prompt)` collapses them. Minimal change: add `PromptDelivery` to `Capabilities`, add a `TurnKind` enum parameter to `continue_turn`, add a `precheck()` hook (default no-op, muse overrides). Do not redesign. Finding #1 (fork drops thread) must be fixed regardless — `engine.rs:361-363`.

## Q3 — Identity newtypes
`ConsultationId/AttemptId/ConversationId` (`engine.rs:124-134`) are transparent string wrappers with no constructors or invariants. Retry-as-new-attempt, http-replay continuation, and never-cross-lineage are stated in docs only and unenforceable here. Acceptable if the runtime owns them, but then the layer should enforce what it can: make constructors private, expose `AttemptId::retry()` (new id, same inputs) and `ConversationId` split (CLI thread vs `HttpTranscript`), and put the lineage-equality check on the resume/fork path. Currently `capabilities().resume/fork` plus `Mode` allow cross-lineage resume by construction. State machines covered: none enforced; transitions unguarded.

## Q4 — Handoff regenerability
